summary: Partial continuation of #1636: retain the twenty foundation items and add fifteen atomic items for the no-index-two-subfield branch of §4 and its original Bombieri–Pila input. There are ten inherited library items, one inherited planned item and twenty-four provisional missing items, each routed once. The new report repairs norm signs, the identity class, lower-degree squarefree substitution and boundary-fiber counting. It expands the restricted torsion argument while retaining the lattice-source dependencies. The final 2020 source comparison, relative genus theory, remaining application branches and final per-item baseline/ownership audit are unresolved. Do not promote this to a complete paper extraction or accepted design.

items.name: Ordinary ideal class group
items.statement: For a number field K with ring of integers O_K, Cl(K) is the multiplicative group of nonzero fractional O_K-ideals modulo nonzero principal fractional ideals.
items.locator: Introduction p.1 and §2 p.4, Taniguchi 2017-02-18 copy
items.note: Inherited from #1636: ClassGroup uses invertible fractional ideals; the Dedekind-domain instance for O_K gives the stated carrier. Not the narrow class group.

items.name: Finiteness of the number-field class group
items.statement: For every number field K, the ordinary ideal class group Cl(O_K) is finite; its cardinality is h(K).
items.locator: Introduction p.1, implicit in h_m(K); §6 p.10
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Finiteness does not supply a degree-uniform torsion estimate.

items.name: Archimedean absolute values
items.statement: M_infinity(K) consists of the archimedean absolute values associated to embeddings K → C; at a complex place use the ordinary complex modulus, not its square.
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Complex places have multiplicity two in the product formula and norm/volume computations.

items.name: Integral discriminant and its absolute value
items.statement: For a number field K, discr(K) is the determinant of the trace pairing on an integral basis; it is nonzero and independent of that basis. Write D_K = |discr(K)|.
items.note: Inherited from #1636. The Lean integer discr is signed; use its absolute value in all real powers.

items.name: Minkowski space with one complex embedding per pair
items.statement: If K has r real and s complex places, embed K into R^r × C^s via its real embeddings and one representative of each complex pair. This real space has dimension n = [K:Q] = r + 2s.
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Use ordinary product measure and explicitly specify the Euclidean norm for successive minima, not the default product sup norm.

items.name: Covolume of the ring of integers
items.statement: In R^r × C^s with ordinary product Lebesgue measure, the mixed embedding of O_K has covolume 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K).
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Do not reuse this constant unchanged for a metric weighting complex coordinates by two.

items.name: Covolume of a fractional ideal
items.statement: For a nonzero fractional ideal J of O_K, covol(mixedEmbedding(J)) = N_abs(J) 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K). For J = I^(-1) this is 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K)/N(I).
items.note: Inherited from #1636. The Lean input is a unit of the fractional-ideal monoid; the inverse case also uses multiplicativity of absolute norm.

items.name: Minkowski convex-body theorem, strict volume form
items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real normed space with additive Haar measure μ, and L a countable additive subgroup with measurable fundamental domain F. A convex symmetric set S with μ(F) 2^(dim E) < μ(S) contains a nonzero point of L.
items.note: Inherited from #1636. The strict theorem alone does not justify a boundary equality.

items.name: Minkowski convex-body theorem, compact boundary form
items.statement: In a nontrivial finite-dimensional real normed space with additive Haar measure, a compact convex symmetric set S with μ(F) 2^(dim E) ≤ μ(S) contains a nonzero point of a countable discrete subgroup L with fundamental domain F.
items.locator: §2 p.4, boundary case of the non-strict bound
items.note: Inherited from #1636. Compactness, discreteness and nontriviality are required.

items.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
items.statement: Every class of a degree-n number field of signature (r,s) contains a nonzero integral ideal I with N(I) ≤ (4/pi)^s (n!/n^n) sqrt(D_K).
items.note: Inherited from #1636. This does not itself bound all archimedean values of a generator of I^m.

items.name: Successive minima
items.statement: For a full lattice Λ in a positive-dimensional Euclidean real space with closed unit ball B, λ_i is the infimum of t > 0 such that Λ ∩ tB spans a real subspace of dimension at least i, for 1 ≤ i ≤ n.
items.locator: Theorems 1.6 and 3.1, pp.3,5; expanded standard definition
items.note: Inherited from #1636: reviewed AUDIT-02 distinguishes these planned definitions and the second theorem from existing Minkowski-first machinery.

items.name: Weighted box and polydisc for a torsion ideal
items.statement: Given K of degree n, m ≥ 1, a nonzero integral ideal I and I^m = (α) with α ≠ 0, set R_v = D_K^(1/(2n)) |α|_v^(-1/m). The product of real intervals [-R_v,R_v] and closed complex discs of radius R_v is compact, symmetric and convex, with volume 2^r pi^s sqrt(D_K)/N(I).
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. A complex disc contributes pi R_v². The body volume is at least 2^n covol(I^(-1)), since pi ≥ 2.

items.name: Small inverse-ideal multiplier
items.statement: Under the balanced-body hypotheses, there exists κ ∈ I^(-1), κ ≠ 0, with |κ|_v ≤ D_K^(1/(2n)) |α|_v^(-1/m) for every infinite place v.
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. Use compact non-strict Minkowski and the fractional-ideal covolume, retaining a nonzero witness.

items.name: Archimedean-balanced generator of a torsion representative
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K and an ideal class of exact order m ≥ 1, there exist a nonzero integral ideal J in the class and nonzero β ∈ O_K with J^m = (β) and |β|_v ≤ D_K^(m/(2n)) for every infinite place v.
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. Construct J = κI and β = ακ^m. The order-dividing variant is extracted separately in this continuation.

items.name: Balanced generator for an order-two class
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K and an ideal class of exact order two, there are a nonzero integral representative J and nonzero β ∈ O_K with J² = (β) and |β|_v ≤ D_K^(1/n) at every infinite place.
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. For all 2-torsion include the identity through balanced-order-dividing. Only |N(β)| = N(J)² is forced; the field norm can be negative.

items.name: Reduced integral basis starting with one
items.statement: For a degree-n number field with n ≥ 2, choose a Z-basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n-1) of O_K ordered by archimedean Euclidean length, with |v_i| ≪_n |v| for nonzero integral v outside the preceding rational span, and |v_1|...|v_(n-1)| comparable to sqrt(D_K) by positive constants depending only on n.
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. Original Siegel proof remains unread. The source prints the comparison only through n−2, then uses it at n−1; certify the full lemma, primitive vector 1, metric and n=2 case. General reduction belongs to GN.1/GN.3.

items.name: Top-coordinate multiplication matrix
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 and a basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n-1), form the symmetric (n−2)-square rational matrix A whose entry a_ij is the coefficient of v_(n−1) in v_i v_j, for 1 ≤ i,j ≤ n−2.
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. This is a coordinate construction on field multiplication, not the trace Gram matrix.

items.name: Nondegeneracy of the top-coordinate multiplication matrix
items.statement: For any degree-n extension K/Q with n ≥ 3 and Q-basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n−1), the top-coordinate multiplication matrix has nonzero determinant.
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. A nonzero kernel vector r in span(v_1,...,v_(n−2)) makes multiplication by r preserve L = span(1,...,v_(n−2)). Since r is not rational, [Q(r):Q] ≥ 2 divides both n and n−1, a contradiction. The permutation term in the nonzero determinant still needs its own proof node at blueprint time.

items.name: Degree-dependent upper bound for the largest minimum
items.statement: For every n ≥ 2 there is C_n > 0 such that every degree-n number field K satisfies λ_n(O_K) ≤ C_n D_K^(1/n) for its archimedean Euclidean lattice. For the controlled reduced basis of §3, also |v_(n−1)| ≪_n D_K^(1/n).
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. For n=2 use the product bound. For n≥3 use a nonzero permutation term, reduction and norm multiplication to obtain |v_(n−1)|^n ≪_n D_K. Still depends on the exact reduced-basis source lemma.

items.name: Coarse count of small algebraic integers
items.statement: For fixed n and c > 0, the number of β ∈ O_K with |β|_v ≤ c D_K^(1/n) at every infinite place is O_(n,c)(D_K^(1/2)), uniformly over degree-n number fields K.
items.note: Inherited author-copy extraction from #1636; comparison with the final 2020 text is still open. Use a uniformly controlled fundamental parallelepiped and disjoint-translate volumes, not a fixed-lattice asymptotic with field-dependent error.

items.name: Balanced generators for classes killed by m
items.statement: Let K be a degree-n number field, m ≥ 1 and c ∈ Cl(K) with c^m = 1. There exist a nonzero integral ideal J representing c and nonzero β ∈ O_K with J^m = (β) and |β|_v ≤ D_K^(m/(2n)) at every infinite place.
items.locator: Theorem 2.1 proof p.4, logical order-dividing extension used in §4
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. The proof uses only I^m principal, not exact order m. This extends rather than misquotes the displayed theorem; in particular it includes the identity class.

items.name: Injecting 2-torsion into balanced square-norm elements
items.statement: For K of degree n set R = D_K^(1/n) and B_K(R) = {β ∈ O_K : |β|_v ≤ R for every infinite v}. Choosing the order-dividing-m=2 representatives defines an injection Cl(K)[2] → {β ∈ B_K(R) : β ≠ 0 and |N_K/Q(β)| is an integer square}.
items.locator: Opening of §4 p.6; injectivity and norm-sign details expanded in this report
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. If two chosen generators agree, their ideal squares agree; unique factorization of nonzero ideals then identifies the ideals and their classes. Use both norm signs.

items.name: A uniform variable-radius integer count
items.statement: For each d ≥ 1 there is C_d such that for every degree-d number field F and every real T ≥ D_F^(1/d), the number of α ∈ O_F with |α|_v ≤ T at every infinite place is at most C_d T^d / sqrt(D_F).
items.locator: §4 p.6, expansion of the subfield-box estimate following Lemma 4.1
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. From the controlled integral basis and largest-minimum theorem, a fundamental parallelepiped lies in a degree-dependent dilation of the T-box. Disjoint translates and covolume prove the bound. Treat F=Q directly.

items.name: The monic integral norm polynomial
items.statement: For β ∈ O_K define P_β(X) as the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by β on the free Z-module O_K. It is monic in Z[X], has degree [K:Q], and satisfies P_β(t) = N_K/Q(t−β) for t ∈ Q.
items.locator: §4 p.6 norm polynomial; monic sign convention expanded here
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. The paper uses N(β−X) = (−1)^n P_β(X). Import the existing characteristic-polynomial, determinant and norm APIs rather than creating duplicate carriers; the packaged comparison has not been matched to an exact pinned declaration.

items.name: Multiplicity of the roots of a norm polynomial
items.statement: Let β ∈ O_K, let q_β ∈ Z[X] be its monic minimal polynomial, and set e = [K:Q(β)]. Then P_β = q_β^e, and every complex root of P_β has multiplicity e.
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. Use restriction of scalars from Q(β) or the norm tower, and separability in characteristic zero. The exponent uses the generated field Q(β), not an arbitrary subfield containing β.

items.name: Square norm polynomials and even generated-field index
items.statement: For β ∈ O_K, P_β is a square in C[X] if and only if [K:Q(β)] is even. In the even case its monic square root lies in Z[X].
items.locator: Lemma 4.1, §4 p.6, with the monic sign convention
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. Apply the root multiplicity statement. For the paper’s signed norm polynomial, being a square may require multiplication by −1.

items.name: Absolute irreducibility of the unreduced norm curve
items.statement: Let K have degree n ≥ 3 and β ∈ O_K with e = [K:Q(β)] odd. For each s ∈ {1,−1}, the affine plane curve Y² − sP_β(X) = 0 is absolutely irreducible of total degree n.
items.locator: §4 p.6, replacement of the squarefree-part step by an unreduced norm curve
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. P_β is not a square in C(X), so the monic quadratic in Y is irreducible there; Gauss’s lemma gives irreducibility in C[X,Y]. Repeated roots can make the curve singular, but do not change total degree or this conclusion. This is an explicit proof repair, not a verbatim named source lemma.

items.name: Counting the even-index exceptional locus
items.statement: Let K have fixed degree n ≥ 3 and no subfield F with [K:F] = 2. Among β ∈ O_K satisfying |β|_v ≤ D_K^(1/n) at every infinite place, the number with [K:Q(β)] even is O_n(D_K^(1/4)).
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. For F=Q(β) its even index e is at least 4. The discriminant tower gives D_F^(e) ≤ D_K, so variable-radius-box-count applies and yields O_n(D_K^(1/e)/sqrt(D_F)). Sum over the bounded number of subfields (for example at most 2^(n!)). In odd degree the exceptional locus is empty. The discriminant and subfield machinery must be imported from its baseline supplier.

items.name: Uniform count of integer-translation classes
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K with n ≥ 3, set R = D_K^(1/n). The number of additive cosets in O_K/Z meeting B_K(R) is O_n(D_K^(1/2−1/n)).
items.locator: Final paragraph of §4 p.6; boundary-safe proof expanded in this report
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. Choose one β_L in each nonempty coset. The pairs (L,m), |m| ≤ floor(R), inject by β_L+m into B_K(2R). Divide the coarse count for the enlarged box by 2 floor(R)+1. Do not assume every fiber inside the original box has length comparable to R.

items.name: Both norm signs in a bounded norm-curve rectangle
items.statement: For K of degree n ≥ 3, R = D_K^(1/n), β_0 ∈ B_K(R) and α = β_0−m ∈ B_K(R) with m ∈ Z, α ≠ 0 and |N(α)| = y² for y ∈ Z_≥0, one has |m| ≤ 2R and 0 < y ≤ sqrt(D_K). The assignment α ↦ (s,m,y), with s chosen so that y² = sP_β0(m), injects into the union of the two norm curves in this rectangle.
items.locator: §4 p.6, with the ± sign made explicit as in §5.1 p.7
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. The sign also incorporates P_β0(m) = (−1)^n N(α). The norm is nonzero. The rectangle fits an integer translate of a square of side at most C_n sqrt(D_K).

items.name: The square-norm saving on one translation class
items.statement: For every n ≥ 3 and ε > 0 there is C_(n,ε) such that, uniformly over degree-n fields K and β_0 ∈ B_K(D_K^(1/n)) with [K:Q(β_0)] odd, the number of nonzero α ∈ (β_0+Z) ∩ B_K(D_K^(1/n)) whose absolute norm is a square is at most C_(n,ε) D_K^(1/(2n)+ε).
items.locator: Final paragraph of §4 p.6, with the unreduced norm-curve repair
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. Apply the coefficient-uniform Bombieri–Pila theorem to each absolutely irreducible degree-n signed curve in a square of side O_n(sqrt(D_K)). Q(β_0+m)=Q(β_0). The proof permits singular curves; it does not give the lower-degree squarefree part the wrong degree n.

items.name: Square-norm count without an index-two subfield
items.statement: For every n ≥ 3 and ε > 0, uniformly over degree-n fields K having no subfield of index two, the number of nonzero β ∈ O_K with |β|_v ≤ D_K^(1/n) at all infinite places and |N(β)| an integer square is O_(n,ε)(D_K^(1/2−1/(2n)+ε)).
items.locator: §4 p.6, expanded combination of the odd- and even-index cases
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. Multiply the translation-coset count by the odd-index bound and add O_n(D_K^(1/4)) for the even-index locus. Since n ≥ 3, that error is absorbed. This proof consumes the recorded lattice lemmas and the original Bombieri–Pila input.

items.name: The general-exponent torsion bound in the no-index-two case
items.statement: For every n ≥ 3 and ε > 0 there is C_(n,ε) such that every degree-n number field K with no subfield F satisfying [K:F]=2 has |Cl(K)[2]| ≤ C_(n,ε) D_K^(1/2−1/(2n)+ε).
items.locator: Theorem 1.1 general exponent and §4 p.6, explicitly restricted to the branch whose proof is expanded here
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. Combine torsion-square-norm-injection with balanced-square-norm-count. This covers odd degrees, but is not the whole theorem for even degrees, nor the sharper cubic/quartic exponent. The relative-genus-theory reduction remains unresolved in this checkpoint.

items.name: Coefficient-uniform Bombieri–Pila plane-curve estimate
items.statement: Let C be an absolutely irreducible affine plane curve of total degree d ≥ 2, and let N ≥ exp(d^6). The number of integral points on C in [0,N] × [0,N] is at most N^(1/d) exp(12 sqrt(d log N log log N)).
items.locator: Bombieri–Pila, The number of integral points on arcs and ovals, Theorem 5, author preprint p.17; cited in BSTTTZ §4 p.6
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. The original theorem and its local concluding proof were read and the formula was visually checked in a PDF screenshot. No smoothness or coefficient-height hypothesis is present. The full preceding determinant-method proof remains to decompose.

items.name: Translated-square epsilon form of Bombieri–Pila
items.statement: For each integer d ≥ 2 and real ε > 0 there is C_(d,ε) such that every absolutely irreducible real plane curve of total degree d has at most C_(d,ε) N^(1/d+ε) integer points in any integer translate of [0,N]², for every N ≥ 1. The constant is independent of the curve coefficients and the translating integers.
items.locator: Elementary consequence of Bombieri–Pila Theorem 5, author preprint p.17; form consumed in BSTTTZ §4
items.note: New continuation, g6ap-0921-classgroup-7c4e. Status and ownership require the final pinned-library/cross-roadmap audit; no implementation absence is certified. For large N absorb the subpower exponential; for the bounded remaining interval use the grid count (floor(N)+1)². Integer translation preserves integral points and total degree.

routes.title: Effective arithmetic bounds and geometry of numbers, Part II: class-group torsion and balanced ideal generators
routes.reason: Continue the provisional #1636 extension without changing the completed parent. Its coarse class-number/ideal bounds do not supply the paper-specific balanced-generator and norm-curve argument. General algebra, reduction and discriminant facts must still be imported, not re-owned. This is not an accepted route or the full paper’s final theorem package.
routes.brief: Provisional continuation brief: settle the final source version and all pinned-library/ownership checks before design intake. Build on Effective arithmetic bounds and geometry of numbers (tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds). Import the existing class group, absolute discriminant, mixed embedding, fractional-ideal covolume, compact Minkowski theorem, characteristic polynomial, norm tower and ideal-factorization APIs. Import general successive minima and reduced-basis theory from Geometry of numbers and quadratic arithmetic GN.1/GN.3, retaining its primitive-vector and last-index obligations. Prove balanced generators for classes killed by m, including the identity, and the largest-minimum and variable-radius box estimates. Construct the injection of 2-torsion into nonzero balanced elements with absolute square norm. Set P_beta(X)=N(X-beta); identify it with the minimal polynomial to the generated-field index, and preserve both norm signs. Import the coefficient-uniform Bombieri–Pila estimate from its actual reusable supplier after the separate provisional counting route is audited. For odd generated-field index apply it to the unreduced, possibly singular norm curve of total degree n; do not replace that curve by a lower-degree squarefree part while retaining exponent 1/n. Count integer-translation cosets by injecting fixed-length translates into the enlarged box. For fields without an index-two subfield, bound the even-index locus via discriminant towers and variable-radius subfield counts, then prove h_2(K) = O_(n,epsilon)(D_K^(1/2-1/(2n)+epsilon)). This is the current restricted endpoint, not the full even-degree theorem or the sharper cubic/quartic bound. Finish the original relative-genus-theory, Selmer, elliptic, quartic, function-field and del Pezzo branches before extending the final targets. Tests include the identity class, negative norms, a rational beta in an odd-degree field giving a singular irreducible curve, and short boundary fibers in the original box. Preserve the earlier Couveignes proposal as an overlap to reconcile, not an installed supplier.

routes.title: Uniform integral-point bounds by determinant methods
routes.reason: The read RP roadmap supplies finiteness, ED supplies certified algorithms, and LD.6 supplies Pila–Wilkie outside the algebraic part; none of those contracts is this coefficient-uniform count on the algebraic curve itself. An exact-ID search found no result, but the full proposed-roadmap/reserved-ID and baseline audit remains required. This reusable owner is provisional.
routes.brief: Provisional reusable counting direction, not a new owner for algebraic geometry or Pila–Wilkie. Read and decompose the complete original Bombieri–Pila proof, with the author preprint version and published comparison recorded. Import finite-dimensional determinants, polynomial evaluation and degree, real differentiation and Rolle-type estimates, and the appropriate existing plane-curve intersection/Bézout supplier. Construct the monomial evaluation matrices, integer nonzero-determinant lower bound, analytic upper bound, covering by auxiliary curves and the uniform treatment of singular points and changes of coordinate.
